questions.text: Consider an undirected graph G where self-loops are not allowed. The vertex set of G is {(i,f):1[latex]\leq[/latex]i[latex]\leq[/latex]12, 1[latex]\leq[/latex]j[latex]\leq[/latex]12}. There is an edge between (a,b) and (c,d) if |a-c|[latex]\leq[/latex]1 and |b-d| [latex]\leq[/latex]1. The number of edges in the graph is ____.
questions.solution:
This is a 12 [latex]\times[/latex] 12 grid where each cell is joined to all 8 neighbours (like king moves):
- horizontal: 12 [latex]\times[/latex] 11 = 132
- vertical: 12 [latex]\times[/latex] 11 = 132
- diagonal (both directions): 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 11 [latex]\times[/latex] 11 = 242

Total = 506

Answer: 506

questions.text: An ordered n-tuple ([latex]d_{1}, d_{2} ,... , d_{n}[/latex]) with [latex]d_{1}\geq d_{2} \geq ... \geq d_{n}[/latex] is called graphic if there exists a simple undirected graph with n vertices having degrees [latex]d_{1}, d_{2} ,... , d_{n}[/latex] respectively. Which of the following 6-tuples is NOT graphic?
questions.solution:
(3, 3, 3, 1, 0, 0): ignore the two isolated vertices, leaving 4 vertices with degrees 3, 3, 3, 1. Each degree-3 vertex must connect to all three others, so the fourth vertex would have degree 3, not 1. Not graphic.

The others are graphic (e.g. three disjoint edges, a 6-cycle, a small tree).

Answer: (3, 3, 3, 1, 0, 0)

questions.text:
Which one of the following propositional logic formulas is TRUE when exactly two of p, q,
and r are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Exactly two true means either r is true with exactly one of p, q (that is [latex]\neg(p\leftrightarrow q)\wedge r[/latex]), or p and q true with r false ([latex]p\wedge q\wedge\sim r[/latex]). Option 2 is exactly the OR of these two cases.

Answer: Option 2

questions.text:
Given the following schema:
employees(emp-id, first-name, last-name, hire-date, dept-id, salary)
departments(dept-id, dept-name, manager-id, location-id)
You want to display the last names and hire dates of all latest hires in their respective departments in the location ID 1700. You issue the following query: 
 SQL>SELECT last-name, hire-date
FROM employees
WHERE (dept-id, hire-date) IN
(SELECT dept-id, MAx(hire-date)
FROM employees JOIN departments USING(dept-id)
WHERE location-id = 1700
GROUP BY dept-id);
What is the outcome?
questions.solution:
The subquery returns, for each department at location 1700, its dept-id and latest hire date. The outer query keeps employees whose (dept-id, hire-date) pair is in that list. Multi-column IN is valid and GROUP BY works in a subquery with a join.

Answer: It executes and gives the correct result

questions.text:
Consider two processors P1 and P2 executing the same instruction set. Assume that under
identical conditions, for the same input, a program running on P2 takes 25% less time but
incurs 20% more CPI (clock cycles per instruction) as compared to the program running on
P1. If the clock frequency of P1 is 1GHz, then the clock frequency of P2 (in GHz) is _________.
questions.solution:
Time = IC [latex]\times[/latex] CPI / f. With [latex]T_2=0.75T_1[/latex] and [latex]CPI_2=1.2\,CPI_1[/latex]:
[latex]0.75=\frac{1.2}{f_2/f_1}\Rightarrow f_2=\frac{1.2}{0.75}\times1=1.6[/latex] GHz

Answer: 1.6
